method: Reviewed LLM-as-a-judge claims and recommendations against Zheng et al.'s MT-Bench paper. Audited the lesson, metadata checkpoint, historical data ledger and the embedded Python example. Executed the offline synthetic example and 10 content/evidence-boundary assertions. No provider or external service calls were made.

observations.trace: The synthetic example kept the same candidate winner across swapped positions for one case, changed winner identity for a same-slot preference case, and rejected the ambiguous label 'A or B'. Historical 0/12, 4/4 and 0/6 figures remain labeled as unverified summaries and are not treated as population bias rates or judge accuracy.

limitations: This was a source and lesson-contract review, not a replication of the historical DeepSeek experiment.
The old per-call responses, full prompts, model snapshot, decoding configuration, human labels and scorer version were not available for independent replay.
No human-reference calibration, benchmark evaluation, cross-model comparison or production judge validation was performed.
The offline example verifies strict label parsing and order comparison only; it says nothing about actual model behavior or correctness.
